function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

### How Turbonomics Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability | Goal | What Turbonomics Provides | Why It Matters for Unilever | |------|---------------------------|-----------------------------| | **Unified Visibility Across All Clouds** | • **Real‑time telemetry collection** from on‑prem, GCP, AWS, Azure, and other SaaS workloads.
• **Single pane of glass** dashboards that aggregate metrics (CPU, memory, I/O, network, cost, SLAs). | Unilever can see the health of every application and infrastructure component in one place, eliminating the “cloud‑silos” problem. | | **AI‑Driven Root‑Cause Analysis** | • Uses machine learning models to correlate performance anomalies with underlying causes (e.g., resource contention, mis‑configured autoscaling).
• Generates automated alerts and remediation suggestions. | Faster incident response, reduced MTTR, and fewer manual investigations. | | **Predictive Capacity Planning** | • Forecasts future demand for compute, storage, and network resources based on historical trends and upcoming business events (seasonal sales, marketing campaigns).
• Suggests optimal sizing and placement across clouds. | Enables Unilever to avoid over‑provisioning (cost savings) while ensuring capacity for peak demand. | | **Cost Optimization & Chargeback** | • Tracks spend per workload, per team, or per product line.
• Applies AI to recommend rightsizing, spot‑instance usage, or reserved‑instance purchases. | Gives Unilever granular cost visibility and actionable recommendations to reduce cloud spend. | | **Policy‑Based Automation** | • Define policies (e.g., “scale up only if CPU > 70% for 5 min”) that are enforced automatically across all clouds.
• Integrates with Terraform, Kubernetes, CloudFormation, etc. | Consistent operational behavior regardless of provider, reducing human error. | | **Compliance & Governance** | • Monitors compliance with internal security and regulatory standards (GDPR, PCI‑DSS, etc.).
• Generates audit reports. | Helps Unilever maintain regulatory compliance across a distributed environment. | #### How Turbonomics Works in Practice 1. **Data Ingestion** – Agents or APIs pull metrics from each cloud provider’s native monitoring services (Stackdriver, CloudWatch, Monitor, etc.) and from on‑prem sources (VMware vSphere, Hyper‑V, etc.). 2. **Normalization** – All metrics are converted into a common schema so they can be compared side‑by‑side. 3. **AI Engine** – A continuously learning model identifies patterns, predicts future states, and recommends actions. 4. **Action Layer** – Recommendations are either auto‑executed (via APIs) or surfaced to operators for approval. 5. **Feedback Loop** – Outcomes of actions feed back into the model, improving accuracy over time. --- ### Difference Between Turbonomics and Native Cloud Observability Tools | Feature | Turbonomics | Native Cloud Tools (GCP, AWS, Azure) | |---------|-------------|-------------------------------------| | **Scope** | Cross‑cloud + on‑prem | Single‑provider | | **Unified Dashboard** | One UI for all clouds | Separate dashboards per provider | | **AI/ML Capabilities** | Predictive analytics, root‑cause AI, automated remediation | Mostly rule‑based alerts; limited predictive ML | | **Cost Management** | Detailed chargeback, rightsizing, reservation optimization | Basic cost explorer; no unified chargeback across clouds | | **Policy Enforcement** | Declarative policies applied across all environments | Policies are provider‑specific (e.g., IAM roles, Security Groups) | | **Automation** | Auto‑scale, auto‑rightsize, auto‑migration suggestions | Manual scaling or provider‑specific automation (e.g., Lambda, Autoscaling groups) | | **Compliance Reporting** | Unified audit logs, policy compliance dashboards | Provider‑specific compliance reports | | **Integration** | Works with Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible, ServiceNow, etc. | Limited to provider SDKs/APIs | | **Learning Curve** | Requires initial setup but offers a single learning path | Multiple learning paths for each provider | #### Bottom Line - **Native tools** give you deep visibility *within* a single cloud but require separate teams, dashboards, and skill sets for each provider. - **Turbonomics** stitches those silos together, adds AI‑driven insight, and automates actions across the entire stack—exactly what Unilever needs to manage its global, multi‑cloud footprint efficiently and cost‑effectively.
